correctness.rationale: PASS: Independently checked proof from the actual binary coding: a unique circle phase exists because each nonzero phase translation changes the interval indicator on an open arc, sampled densely by irrational rotation. Phase fibers are singleton except endpoint orbits; one-sided limits differ at one time if boundary orbits differ, at two times separated by |k| otherwise. Every winning schedule must hit all translates of [-R,R] or the union of two such intervals. Every nonempty periodic covering schedule separates distinct phases by density of each arithmetic progression n≡r mod period, and separates same-phase endpoints by covering, establishing equality with κ. A finite 2^(q+2R)-state de Bruijn graph attains the covering min mean on a cycle. For q=5,R=1, independently constructed 128 vertices and 252 edges; integer Bellman-Ford relaxation has no negative cycle at cost 11b−2, and a 2/11 period11 schedule covers all shifts. Bounds and algorithm are exact; finite graph is not a proof of irrational phase dynamics.
